value: Deep learning MRI brain tumor classification

objective.value: Classify MRI brain scans into glioma, meningioma, pituitary, or no tumor, and expose predictions through an interactive Streamlit app with visual explanations.

repositoryNote.value: Public repository with Training/ and Testing/ image sets, saved model weights, Streamlit app.py, and saliency_maps/ artifacts.

measuredOutcomes.value: Repository README states custom CNN 98% test accuracy and Xception transfer-learning 99% test accuracy. Figures are author-published in-repo; not independently re-measured in Discovery.

problem.value: Assist early detection workflows by classifying MRI brain scans into glioma, meningioma, pituitary, or no tumor, with a path from trained models to an interactive prediction UI.

overview.value: Deep learning MRI tumor classification using a fine-tuned Xception model and a custom Keras CNN, exposed through a Streamlit app that accepts uploads and shows predictions with saliency-map explanations (Gemini 1.5 Flash integrated per README).

architecture.value: Two model paths: ImageNet-pretrained Xception fine-tuned for four-class MRI classification, and a custom CNN built in Keras. Streamlit app.py loads saved weights (cnn_model.h5, xception_model.weights.h5), runs inference on uploaded scans, and produces saliency visualizations under saliency_maps/. stages: Load saved weights, Run inference on uploaded scans, Produce saliency visualizations.

decisions.value: Compare transfer learning (Xception) against a custom CNN in the same product surface so both prediction paths are available in the Streamlit app rather than shipping a single opaque model.

constraints.value: Depends on Training/ and Testing/ MRI datasets and pre-trained weight files committed or referenced in the repository for app inference.
